investorTypes.name: Venture Capital Firms
investorTypes.description: Professional investment firms that manage pooled capital from limited partners to invest in high-growth startups. They are the most active lead investors in AI and participate across every stage from seed to growth.
investorTypes.aiRelevance: Primary source of capital for foundation-model labs, AI infrastructure, and vertical AI applications.

investorTypes.name: Corporate Venture Capital
investorTypes.description: Investment arms of large corporations. They invest to acquire strategic technology, secure supply chains, and build ecosystems around their core products.
investorTypes.aiRelevance: Cloud providers, chipmakers, and enterprise software giants use CVC to secure AI talent and distribution.

investorTypes.name: Family Offices
investorTypes.description: Private wealth-management arms of high-net-worth families. Single-family offices (SFOs) and multi-family offices (MFOs) are increasingly writing direct checks into AI startups.
investorTypes.aiRelevance: Flexible, long-term capital that can participate in hot AI rounds without LP reporting constraints.

investorTypes.name: Industry Funds
investorTypes.description: Sector-focused funds backed by governments or industry associations. They aim to build domestic capabilities in strategic technologies.
investorTypes.aiRelevance: Often deployed to localize AI supply chains, semiconductors, and sovereign infrastructure.

investorTypes.name: Individual Angel Investors
investorTypes.description: High-net-worth individuals who invest personal capital at the earliest stages. Many AI angels are former founders, researchers, or operators with deep technical credibility.
investorTypes.aiRelevance: Critical for pre-product AI labs where technical due diligence matters more than financial metrics.

investorTypes.name: Angel Syndicates & Rolling Funds
investorTypes.description: Groups of individual angels who pool capital behind a lead investor. Platforms like AngelList and Carta allow operators to run small, thesis-driven funds.
investorTypes.aiRelevance: Enables operator-investors to back niche AI tools and open-source projects that traditional VCs may overlook.

investorTypes.name: Private Equity
investorTypes.description: Funds that acquire or invest in more mature companies, often with a focus on profitability, recurring revenue, and operational improvement.
investorTypes.aiRelevance: PE is moving into AI-enabled vertical software, data assets, and take-private opportunities.

investorTypes.name: Sovereign Wealth Funds
investorTypes.description: State-owned investment funds that manage national savings. They are patient, long-term capital sources that often anchor mega-rounds.
investorTypes.aiRelevance: Major backers of AI unicorns and compute-heavy infrastructure plays requiring patient capital.

investorTypes.name: Government Guidance Funds
investorTypes.description: Public-sector vehicles designed to stimulate domestic innovation, attract talent, and secure strategic technology leadership.
investorTypes.aiRelevance: Used to anchor AI clusters, national labs, and startups with local job-creation obligations.

investorTypes.name: Accelerators & Incubators
investorTypes.description: Programs that provide seed capital, mentorship, and network access in exchange for a small equity stake. Some also run follow-on funds.
investorTypes.aiRelevance: Massive feeder system for AI-native startups; many top AI labs trace back to YC and EF cohorts.

investorTypes.name: Fund of Funds
investorTypes.description: Investors that allocate capital to other VC, PE, and hedge funds rather than investing directly in startups.
investorTypes.aiRelevance: Indirectly increases AI allocation by backing specialist AI-focused VC managers.

investorTypes.name: Endowments & University Funds
investorTypes.description: Long-term capital pools owned by universities and non-profits. They typically invest in VC funds and occasionally co-invest.
investorTypes.aiRelevance: Patient, mission-aligned capital that can support AI research spinouts and deep-tech funds.

investorTypes.name: Pension Funds & Insurers
investorTypes.description: Large institutional investors with long liabilities. They enter AI through private-market fund commitments and crossover rounds.
investorTypes.aiRelevance: Increasingly participating in AI growth rounds as the asset class matures and generates revenue.

investorTypes.name: Hedge Funds & Crossover Investors
investorTypes.description: Public-market investors that also deploy capital into private companies ahead of an anticipated IPO or crossover event.
investorTypes.aiRelevance: Often lead rapid, large AI rounds based on public-market comparables and momentum.

investorTypes.name: Strategic Investors & Ecosystem Partners
investorTypes.description: Companies that invest directly in startups to lock in supply, distribution, or product integration. Unlike CVC, these may not be formal venture arms.
investorTypes.aiRelevance: Common in AI infrastructure, where compute credits, distribution, and co-development are as valuable as cash.

investorTypes.name: Crowdfunding & Community Rounds
investorTypes.description: Platforms that allow a large number of smaller investors to participate, often through SAFEs or revenue-sharing instruments.
investorTypes.aiRelevance: Useful for consumer AI tools and AI creator platforms that can build a community of early adopters.

investorTypes.name: Development Finance Institutions
investorTypes.description: Multilateral banks and development agencies that invest in projects with social, environmental, or developmental impact.
investorTypes.aiRelevance: Emerging source for AI applied to climate, health, education, and financial inclusion in developing markets.
